lines: Did anyone mistake anger for courage during the trouble at Deep Dark?
{target}? Sound travels farther than sense.
Whose plan got the group safely past Deep Dark?
Did anyone have to share tools after something broke at Deep Dark?
Before searching anything, I would make certain I could still find a wool-marked path back to the surface.
The Warden would make me think twice before drawing steel.
That makes Deep Dark sound like darkness that listens back.
I would rather repair a weapon from Deep Dark than replace its owner.
Could you keep steady footing while moving through Deep Dark?
Your tale has me reconsidering a short blade kept clear of the walls. Perhaps reach is not always the answer.
Bring me the gear afterward. I want to check for sculk dust packed into the guard before it gets worse.
Of everything you described, one careless noise waking the whole place worries me most.
The market may value echo shards and old enchanted gear. I value seeing the traveler return.
Sculk hears what pride forgets.
I would slow down around sculk-lined caverns below the world. Hurrying there sounds expensive.
I would like to inspect the grip that carried you through Deep Dark.
Could you tell where the <shake>danger</shake> was by listening at Deep Dark?
Even a weaponsmith knows when shelter matters more than steel. I would look for a sealed side room away from shriekers.
If anyone heads for Deep Dark, tell them. Walk soft and do not open every chest.
Did you take every footstep carrying through the dark as a warning, or did it only make the place worse?
The first thing on my bench would be any piece affected by mineral grit scoring the edge.
Pointed stone makes every stumble serious.
If anyone heads for Dripstone Caves, tell them. Look up as often as you look down.
Was the loudest moment at Dripstone Caves part of the fight or the escape?
Did finding copper and stone between the spikes justify the <shake>danger</shake> once you finally saw it?
If trouble closed in, I hope you fell back toward the widest ledge toward the entrance.
Was there a moment at Dripstone Caves when standing firm became foolish?
That makes Dripstone Caves sound like a cave that bites from both directions.
A fine weapon means little when you cannot plant your feet around caverns lined with pointed stone above and below.
What would you change about your gear before seeing Dripstone Caves again?
Hearing about Dripstone Caves reminds me why balance matters more than shine.
Did anything at Dripstone Caves sound harmless before it attacked?
{target}? Stone teeth hang above and wait below.
I hope you found a dry shelf clear of falling dripstone before exhaustion made the choices for you.
Against zombies among the columns, I would trust a short sword that will not catch on stone only after every way around had failed.
Was a stumble turning into a fall on spikes the moment you nearly turned back?
Did the surroundings at Dripstone Caves hide danger until it was close?
If I armed someone for the same road, I would start with a short sword that will not catch on stone.
Could the damaged weapon still be trusted on the way home from Dripstone Caves?
I can almost hear water drops masking small movements from the way you tell it.
Which warning sound at Lush Caves came just in time?

Did you carry anything sharp that never left its sheath at Lush Caves?
Did the edge stay sharp through everything at Lush Caves?

If anyone heads for Lush Caves, tell them. Watch the vines and the holes between them.

I can prepare steel for impact. I cannot prepare a traveler for a vine lowering someone over a hidden drop.
Zombies beneath the glow berries would make me think twice before drawing steel.

{target}? Pretty caves still have long drops.
Glow berries light paths that may not be safe.

Did you take water and leaves hiding approaching steps as a warning, or did it only make the place worse?
The market may value glow berries, clay, and flowering plants. I value seeing the traveler return.
A weapon only buys choices when trouble closes in around Lush Caves.
